findings.title: Backup code consumption is not atomic, allowing replay
findings.body: The code checks the backup code index, then later writes back the re-encrypted array with the used code nulled, in a separate non-transactional update. Two concurrent login requests with the same valid backup code can both pass the indexOf check before either write lands, so one backup code can be used twice. The code is single-use by design, so this breaks the security guarantee.

findings.title: Used backup code is set to null, but indexOf of a null entry and remaining codes are not validated
findings.body: Setting backupCodes[index] = null keeps the array length, and the stored JSON contains nulls. Submitting an empty or whitespace string after replaceAll can match a null entry only if the input is null, which is not possible from a string, so this is mostly safe, but a user submitting an input that is the empty string bypasses the check because credentials.backupCode is falsy and falls back to TOTP. More concretely, the truthiness check on backupCode means an attacker-supplied backupCode of an empty string skips backup verification entirely; the backup-code path is only reached when the field is non-empty.

findings.title: Backup code verification is not consumed and the disable path accepts an unvalidated body value
findings.body: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll is called on a value that may not be a string (JSON body can send a number or object), which throws a 500 instead of a clean error. Also the used backup code is never consumed here, but the subsequent update wipes all backup codes anyway, so this is acceptable only if disabling is the sole consumer; the reliance on the later update is implicit and fragile.

findings.title: JSON.parse of decrypted backup codes can throw unhandled
findings.body: If the stored backupCodes is corrupted or the decryption key changed, symmetricDecrypt or JSON.parse throws, producing an unhandled exception and a 500 with no ErrorCode. The same unguarded parse exists in next-auth-options.ts authorize, where it aborts login with an unmapped error.

findings.title: Setup overwrites existing backup codes before enable, invalidating the previous set on abandoned setup
findings.body: Backup codes are written to the DB at setup time while twoFactorEnabled is still false. If the user abandons enrollment, the previously stored codes are replaced anyway, and the codes shown to the user are only persisted, not confirmed. Also, codes are generated even if the user never completes the TOTP step, so the displayed codes can be out of sync with what is stored if setup is called twice (the second call overwrites the first set the user may have already saved).

findings.title: backupCodes state typed as untyped empty array
findings.body: useState([]) infers never[] under strict typing and the later assignment from body.backupCodes is untyped (any), weakening type safety for the displayed and downloaded codes.

findings.title: Blob URL created on every setup call but revoked only against stale state
findings.body: backupCodesUrl is read from closure state inside handleSetup, so if the user retries setup in the same render cycle the revoke may target a stale URL and leak or revoke the wrong object URL. The download link may then point to a revoked URL.

findings.title: Backup code errors are shown via next-auth result but the error message path for SecondFactorRequired still relies on ErrorCode mapping that drops IncorrectBackupCode in errorMessages
findings.body: The new branches set error text directly, but the Lost access flow never resets twoFactorRequired on credential errors, and when a backup code is wrong the TwoFactor totp input is not shown, so the user cannot see the field they must fix. The error message localization keys are also added only to en/common.json, so other locales fall back to raw keys.

findings.title: No test covers backup code login, the core feature of this PR
findings.body: The only tests exercise TOTP enable and disable plus backup download UI. Nothing verifies that a backup code logs in, that a used code is rejected on reuse, or that a wrong code shows the new error. The TODO acknowledges this, yet the PR checklist claims no tests were added.

findings.title: Backup codes stored as encrypted blob in plain TEXT column without versioning
findings.body: The codes are JSON encrypted with the global CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Rotating the key makes all stored backup codes unreadable, and the authorize and disable paths throw an internal error rather than prompting regeneration. No migration path or key rotation handling is provided.

findings.title: Unrelated tabIndex change on password visibility toggle
findings.body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide password button in the shared PasswordField removes it from keyboard tab order across the whole app, an accessibility regression unrelated to backup codes and not described in the PR.
